drafted_from: tool:google-account-clear_primary_signature's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Clear the signature on my primary send-as address sam@example.com. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-clear_primary_signature as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Clear the signature on my primary send-as address sam@example.com." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-clear_primary_signature, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"send_as_email":"sam@example.com"}.

3. Read what comes back: the request goes as PATCH  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/settings/sendAs/sam@example.com with the body {"signature":""} (body_template is the constant empty string).
4. Run tool:google-account-list_send_as first and copy the sendAsEmail whose isPrimary is true; aliases are not managed by this tool.
